assessment: The statute starts the one-year deletion period after the relevant measure ends and expressly extends the legal permission to continued AI operation. The rationale states the ongoing-operation clock starts only when the data cease to be needed for proper operation. DSTG itself accurately describes the end-of-development/review trigger on physical4. Its annual-data-reduction wording on physical5 could therefore be loose shorthand for successive completed measures rather than a claim of calendar-year purges during necessary operation. The following retrospective judicial/audit concern can also extend beyond ongoing technical necessity. Those affirmative contextual alternatives prevent treating the broadest reading as a proved draft-description error.
materiality: If the universal continuing-use deletion interpretation were established, it could materially support a retention amendment. Current evidence does not establish that intended interpretation, and no legal finding on permissible retention or technical necessity is made.
direction: Recommend null for the unresolved record. A proved exaggerated annual purge would favour longer retention, but a conditional possible direction should be recorded in explanation rather than treated as an established true field.
limits: Does not establish that the proposed rule is ideal, that original training data are never needed for retrospective audits, or that three years is necessary or sufficient.
Does not determine scientific claims about bias, drift or mathematical validity. Those require separate scoped technical investigation.
Does not resolve tax-AI high-risk classification; tax02is a distinct citation issue.
